skill.name: scientific-visualization
skill.description: Create publication-ready scientific figures with matplotlib, seaborn, and plotly. Use journal styles, accessible palettes, multi-panel layouts, and export settings.
skill.summary: Create accessible, journal-ready scientific figures with Python plotting tools.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown backticks, plotting terminology, a comment URL, and dictionary key listings. One medium filesystem risk remains: scripts/style_presets.py can write a caller-supplied style file path. No evidence found for prompt injection, credential access, network execution, or data exfiltration intent.

remediation.issue: Caller-controlled style file output path can overwrite local files.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict create_style_template to a safe output directory, require a .mplstyle suffix, and avoid overwriting existing files without confirmation.

- `apply_publication_style()`: Apply preset styles (default, nature, science, cell)
- Run directly: `python scripts/style_presets.py` to see examples

medium_findings.title: Python file write/append
medium_findings.confidence_reasoning: The helper opens a caller-supplied output_file with write mode to create a matplotlib style file. This is intended functionality, but it can overwrite local files if used with an unsafe path.

content.value_statement: Scientific figures often fail journal standards for size, color, and export format. This skill guides publication-ready plotting with accessible palettes, layouts, and export settings.
actual_capabilities: Guides creation of publication-quality matplotlib, seaborn, and plotly figures.
Provides colorblind-friendly palettes and colormap selection guidance.
Explains multi-panel layouts, error bars, labels, and typography.
Includes helper scripts for journal style presets and figure export.
Lists DPI, file format, and figure width requirements for common journals.
Offers examples for line plots, heatmaps, statistical plots, and multi-panel figures.
limitations: Does not verify journal rules against live publisher websites.
Requires Python plotting libraries in the user environment.
Helper scripts write files only when invoked by the user or agent.
Does not validate statistical methods beyond visualization guidance.

use_cases.title: Prepare Manuscript Figures
use_cases.description: Create figures that match journal size, format, resolution, and typography requirements.

use_cases.title: Standardize Lab Plotting
use_cases.description: Apply consistent palettes, fonts, error bars, and export settings across project figures.

use_cases.title: Review Figure Accessibility
use_cases.description: Check plots for colorblind-safe palettes, grayscale readability, and clear redundant encoding.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Figure
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for one publication-ready plot.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a publication-ready line plot for my data. Use clear labels, units, error bars, and a colorblind-safe palette.

prompt_templates.title: Match Journal Requirements
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for a target journal.
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare this figure for Nature submission. Set the figure width, font sizes, export formats, and DPI for a single-column figure.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Multi-Panel Figure
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a four-panel scientific figure with consistent styling, panel labels, shared legends, and readable text at final print size.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an Existing Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request to improve current plotting code.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my plotting workflow for publication readiness. Identify problems with colors, layout, typography, statistics, and export settings.

output_examples.input: Make a Nature-ready treatment comparison figure with individual points and summary statistics.
output: A single-column figure plan with journal width and readable text sizes.
A colorblind-safe palette with individual data points plus summary error bars.
Export guidance for vector and high-resolution raster formats.

output_examples.input: Check whether my heatmap is suitable for a manuscript.
output: A recommendation to use a perceptually uniform or centered diverging colormap.
A reminder to include a labeled colorbar and readable tick labels.
Accessibility checks for grayscale and color vision deficiency.

output_examples.input: Convert three separate plots into one manuscript figure.
output: A multi-panel layout with consistent axes, spacing, and panel labels.
Shared styling guidance for fonts, line widths, and legends.
A final checklist for journal export and caption consistency.

best_practices: Start with the target journal before choosing figure size and export formats.
Use colorblind-safe palettes and add markers, line styles, or labels for redundancy.
Verify readability at final print size before submission.
anti_patterns: Do not use rainbow or red-green colormaps for critical scientific comparisons.
Do not export plots as low-resolution JPEG files for manuscripts.
Do not rely on summary bars without showing uncertainty or individual data when needed.

faq.question: Which plotting libraries does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers matplotlib, seaborn, and plotly for scientific publication figures.

faq.question: Can it create journal-specific exports?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides guidance and helper scripts for common journal formats, DPI values, and figure widths.

faq.question: Does it make figures colorblind-friendly?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends accessible palettes, perceptually uniform colormaps, and redundant visual encodings.

faq.question: Does it run statistical tests?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on visual presentation, uncertainty display, and figure standards.

faq.question: Can it improve existing plots?
faq.answer: Yes. It can review plots for labels, layout, typography, colors, resolution, and export settings.

faq.question: Does it need internet access?
faq.answer: No. The included guidance and helper scripts are local, but journal rules may change over time.
